emily: Heads-up — AtlasCloud reported a production inference failure for marketplace listing. They're asking for an ops lane. Do we want a shared channel or a private bridge?

mike: Shared channel if they can redactsensitive data. Private Zoom bridge if privacy reqs. what's their preference? @olivia? :thinking_face:

olivia: They prefer shared slack for speed but legal asked to avoid logs in-channel. We can do shared channel + docs link.

emily: Ok. Proposed convention: create ephemeral channel `#partner-atlascloud-sev` and pin a sanitized incident doc. If we need a bridge we'll spin one up. Thoughts?

chris: Agree. Also recommend a short war-room template pinned with roles: triage lead, eng liaison, partner liaison, and escalation owner. e.g.:

```
War room template:
- triage: @sushant
- eng liaison: @mike
- partner liaison: @olivia
- escalation owner: @emily
- short-id: atlas-2025-03-21-01
```

sushant: I'll be triage. Quick ask — what should the oncall handback look like? We had confusion last week about who owns the fallback model routing.

emily: Good call. Handback checklist (short):
- confirm root cause category (runtime / infra / model mismatch)
- confirm mitigations applied (rollback, routing rules, rate-limit)
- agree SLA for follow-up and where postmortem will live
- handback ack from partner liaison

olivia: I'll own partner ack. Can someone paste the sanitized log link here so I can share with AtlasCloud?

mike: Adding link to docs (sanitized): https://internal.redwood/partners/atlascloud/atlas-2025-03-21-01/logs-redacted 

oncall-bot: New channel created: #partner-atlascloud-sev by emily at 1749994020

sushant: Channel exists. I'm pulling traces now. If infra looks healthy we'll try a quick model fallback to v2-quant and monitor.

chris: For routing/fallback, recommend this policy snippet to put in the channel pinned msg:

```
Fallback policy:
- If latency > 800ms for 5m -> switch request routing to v2-quant (canary 10%)
- If errors > 3% for 3m -> full rollback to v1-stable and notify partner
- If cost spike detected -> throttle background batches, keep realtime at 90%
```

emily: Perfect. @mike please update the pinned war-room template with the policy and add a line about customer communications cadence (every 30m until stable).

mike: Done. Pinned and added a short status stanza: `Status 11:40 UTC — investigating, fallback queued`.

olivia: I'm on the call with AtlasCloud ops lead — they're good with the shared channel + sanitized logs. Will relay customer-facing message template after we have a mitigation.

sushant: Traces show a kv-cache pressure spike around 11:33. Applying a conservative cache eviction config now. Will report back in 5m.

emily: Thanks all. After stabilization let's run a 1hr postmortem sync with AtlasCloud and add follow-ups to the partner success playbook. :thumbsup:

chris: Noted. I'll start a short incident tracker in the channel and link to the postmortem doc once we have a timeline.

oncall-bot: Incident status changed to INVESTIGATING at 1749994120

sushant: Eviction change applied. Preliminary metrics show error rate dropping to 0.4% and p95 latency down 20%.

emily: Great progress. Keep updates short and in-channel. We'll escalate to a bridge if customer requests real-time audio.

olivia: Customer thanks the team — will wait for final confirmation before sending formal notice.

mike: If anyone needs to reuse the naming convention, use this pattern: `#partner-<partner>-sev` and warroom id `partner-YYYYMMDD-##`. Keeps things searchable.

emily: Closing notes: we'll draft a short runbook addendum after this. Thanks everyone.
